title: Local git hooks must not slow the dev workflow
goal: CEO 2026-11-11: "the local githooks should not slow dev workflow". Measured on Linux (2026-11-11, loaded host): pre-commit 8-11 s per Rust commit (cargo fmt --all --check over the whole workspace); post-commit ran sync-branch, a network fetch (~0.6 s) plus an automatic merge of origin/main into the branch on every commit (it also pulled unqualified main into release/v0.21.54); pre-push refused every plain git push when push-policy was not installed. Now: pre-commit checks only the staged Rust files with rustfmt and their crate's edition (~0.6 s, most of it the workflow-guard probe) and falls back to the full cargo fmt only when that fast check fails, so it never refuses what cargo fmt accepts; post-commit does no network or merge work (~55 ms; sync-primary stays a throttled background fetch) and sync-branch is retired (branches reconcile at local-snapshot submit); pre-push keeps push-policy's transport safety but finds it on PATH or in the checkout's target, or builds it once offline, failing closed only when it cannot be built.
